speaker: Patient
text: 9-month-old infant. The patient is brought in due to a generalized nonpruritic rash for 2 days. The rash started on the trunk and spread to the extremities. Five days ago, the patient had a fever of 40.5°C (104.9°F) and experienced a 1-minute generalized tonic-clonic seizure. The infant was born at term, has no history of serious illness, and her immunizations are up to date. The current medication includes acetaminophen.

speaker: Doctor
text: Did the high fever resolve abruptly just before the rash appeared? Also, does the infant appear well-appearing and playful now that the fever has broken?

speaker: Doctor
text:
Yes, the fever resolved abruptly, and the infant is now well-appearing and playful. The rash consists of pink, blanching macules.

The clinical presentation of a high fever followed by abrupt defervescence and the appearance of a generalized macular rash is classic for roseola infantum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Roseola Infantum (Exanthem Subitum)
